R61 report only, nothing written; GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md and register_exclusion.json UNTOUCHED. Method pre-registered in a SEPARATE prior commit (3b6825a). ITEM 1 replacement maxDF* baseline, fitted on clean post-R29 (fountain_insight >= 2026-08-09, n=481, 432 rolling windows): median 16% (was 12), p90 20% (was 18), p99 22% (UNCHANGED), max 24%, proposed threshold 24% per the committed rule (R31-consistent alternative 25%; both give 0/432 breaches and both still catch a societal-scale 26-34% event). Live reading under the provisional refit: 16% driven by 'based', vs 30% 'item' on the shipped list. Regime check cleared FIRST: R57 moved doc length only +1.9 content tokens (+6.9%, 0.10 sd) vs R29's +189%, so pooling is safe. PROVISIONAL: n=481 is 48% of the 1000 floor. KEY: term retention already clears R31's 33/40 bar at n~240 (34-39/40) but QUANTILES do not (disjoint first-half fit gives p99 26%), so the 1000-doc floor gates the quantiles, not the list -- a distinction never drawn before. Corrects R60: p99 is unchanged, so the hazard is confined to the median/p90 comparison band, not the alarm ceiling. ITEM 2 citation-chain sweep, 55 candidate lines enumerated: VERDICT EMERGING PATTERN -- 3 additional qualifying chains (2 if self-citation discounted; both in the 2-3 band). A: the ~1000-doc floor itself (R50 -> R51/R53/R58/R59/R60, six rounds, never re-measured, gated the refit ~10 days). B: 99.97% F2 variance (R39 -> R40/R50). C: 9.6->27.7 tokens/doc (R50 -> R59/R60; re-measured here at 27.6, held). NOT systemic -- three other chains WERE refreshed (78/day -> 64.7 -> 79.5; 99.3% edges -> 99.36%; 61.7% tier-6 -> corrected). Failure mode is treating a DERIVED STATISTICAL PROPERTY as a constant; rates and counts self-correct.

R62 report only, nothing written; register_exclusion.json, GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md, corpus_convergence.py all UNTOUCHED. Criterion pre-registered in a SEPARATE prior commit (985b250). VERDICT: NO SHIP. PRIMARY FAILS -- half-vs-half retention (two disjoint halves each fitted independently, compared to each other) min 27/40, best 32/40, bar 33/40; not one of 7 splits clears. This OVERTURNS R61: its 34-39/40 was measured fit-vs-full-corpus where resamples share docs with the reference; R61 flagged the limitation in a caveat then let the headline rest on it. The 1000-doc floor gates BOTH list and quantiles, not quantiles alone. Other three criteria PASS: isolation RE-VERIFIED from scratch (zero importers of corpus_convergence, zero readers of register_exclusion.json outside it, no cron, no systemd) -- R50's four-round-old claim still true; no automated value would move; reversible. So interim risk was never the blocker: post-refit readings mis-locate ~4 pts vs the old band but CANNOT false-breach (max 24% < 25%, 0/433 windows). NEW: the register is NOT STATIONARY -- time-ordered splits 24-27/40 vs random at matched n ~29-31; that gap is drift, not sampling noise, and more docs do not remove drift. Aug 21 clearing 33/40 is BORDERLINE, not assured (extrapolates to ~31-33). R57 is NOT a vocabulary regime break (26/40 across it, vs 24/40 within-regime time splits) so DO NOT restrict the fit to post-R57 -- that would push the floor to ~08-23 for no benefit; ~08-21 stands. R49's spurious-breach mode tested and does NOT reproduce: all 26 dropped v2 terms sit at DF <= 6.2% under a 7.3% floor ('news' 4.6%), and no dropped term is among the live drivers. REFIT ROUND: treat 08-21 as the earliest date to RE-RUN the 7-split gate, not as a ship date.

R63 report only, nothing written; register_exclusion.json, GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md, corpus_convergence.py UNTOUCHED. Discriminator pre-registered in a SEPARATE prior commit (b419c39). VERDICT 1: TREND, not punctuated -- Spearman rho(R,lag) = -0.645 p~0 over 120 disjoint pairs, retention decays smoothly 24.0/21.3/20.1 by lag bucket; best single change-point buys only dR2 = +0.085 vs a 0.15 bar and lands 08-11 04:30, not aligned with R29/contamination-end/R57. Power floor PASSED (120 pairs >= 15, 96 lags >= 3). DRIFT RATE 1.75 of 40 terms lost per day of separation; slope does NOT shrink with window size (-1.40 at W=60, -1.68 at W=100, -2.31 at W=160). VERDICT 2: RED -- plain n=1000 NOT worth trying. Projected R(500) = 25.0/40 vs RED bar <33; drift penalty +5.5 to +6.1 vs RED bar >=5; both fire independently. STRUCTURAL REASON: at 81 docs/day every added document buys sample size AND costs elapsed time -- W 100->500 gains +10.4 to sampling and loses -7.5 to drift, nearly cancelling. To hit 33/40 by throughput needs ~271-411 docs/day vs actual 81 (3.3-5x), and R58 pinned volume at ~82/day. ALSO FAILS: decaying-weight fit (the pre-registration's own named remedy for TREND) ceilings at ~26.1/40 at optimal half-life 2.5d; smaller K is worse fractionally (57.8% at K=10 vs 65.6% at K=40); DF-threshold instead of rank cutoff does not beat it (Jaccard 0.483 vs 0.490) -- my musical-chairs hypothesis was wrong. WHAT WORKS: persistence filtering, terms in the top-40 of ALL k disjoint sub-windows -- survival 67.5% (k=1) / 82.6% (k=2) / 83.3% (k=3) / 92.3% (k=4) vs R31's 82.5% rate bar; trades list size 40/23/18/13 for stability. NOT a drop-in: smaller exclusion set raises readings, so list+quantiles+threshold must be derived together. NEXT IS A DESIGN ROUND, NOT A WAIT.

R64 design round, report only, nothing written; register_exclusion.json, GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md, corpus_convergence.py UNTOUCHED, no list recommended. Design pre-registered in a SEPARATE prior commit (78ccfe1) including an explicit failure clause and anti-tuning clause. VERDICT: PERSISTENCE FILTERING FAILS. Two of three pre-registered failure conditions fire at BOTH k, independently. (b) UNDER-EXCLUSION k=3 80.7%, k=4 91.1% vs a >=50% bar -- excluding the top-18 promotes term #19; 'systems' drives 110/192 held-out windows at k=3, 'engagement' 132 at k=4, same defect as today's 'item' at 30%. (c) SENSITIVITY -- the <=1% false-breach threshold lands at 28% (k=3) and 30% (k=4), both at/above the 26% floor set by the documented societal convergence, so the alarm would not have caught the one real convergence on record. (a) reading agreement PASSES at 2.00pp both -- and it is worthless: the lists agree because they are EQUALLY BLIND, both readings driven by the same unexcluded register token. My own pre-registered bar is necessary but NOT sufficient, found by running it. OVER-EXCLUSION was clean (no 'societal', 1-3 spike flags) exactly as predicted structurally, so the failure is entirely under-exclusion. ITEM 3 ANSWERED, third pre-registered outcome: term retention is the WRONG PROXY and is retired -- retention and reading agreement move in OPPOSITE directions (k=3 55.6%/2.00pp vs top-40 67.5%/4.00pp). Replacement criterion: reading agreement CONDITIONAL ON low under-exclusion; either alone is gameable by a degenerate list (a frozen list scores 0.00pp against itself by construction). BIGGEST FINDING, outranks the k question: under-exclusion does NOT fall with list size -- 27.6% at top-40, 39.6% at top-200, plateauing 25-40%, with 'nature'/'chill' still driving readings at 200 terms excluded. A list fitted on past documents cannot cover a register that drifts at 1.75 terms/day (R63). THE EXCLUSION-LIST APPROACH HAS NO BOTTOM; maxDF*'s core assumption of an enumerable stationary register is false post-R29. Anti-tuning clause HELD: tested k=3 and k=4 only, no others; the top-K sweep is a diagnostic, not a candidate. No replacement mechanism proposed -- design question reopens and any successor needs its own pre-registration.

R65 reopen round, report only, nothing written/deleted; register_exclusion.json, GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md, corpus_convergence.py UNTOUCHED. Pre-registered in a SEPARATE prior commit (6c11814) with retirement on equal terms and a named condition that would block it. VERDICT: REPLACE -- retirement is OFF, and the blocking condition I fixed in advance is what fired. (b) DETECTION PASS: maxDF* CAUGHT the Gatwick convergence -- 42 breaching windows in-window driven by 'societal', peak 34% at 08-04 13:17. NOTE a self-correction: my first replay sampled daily at midnight and reported MISSED; the documented peak is at 13:17, between samples. Per-belief resolution (how the metric actually rolls) gives DETECTED. SPECIFICITY is the real defect: PRECISION 10.8%, 348 of 390 breaches false, every false one register (item 283, discusses 40, aligns 11, engagement 10) vs societal 42 true. (a) UTILITY: ZERO decisions changed -- R36 explained, R49 corroborated, R50 was maintenance of the metric itself, R46/R52 tripwires never evaluated. (c) REDUNDANCY: NOT covered -- groove_alerts ran 126.5/day BEFORE the contamination, 33.2/day DURING, 66.0/day after, i.e. it moved the wrong way; groove detects repeated phrasing, not subject convergence. REPLACEMENT VALIDATED, needs NO exclusion list: self-referencing excess = DF(t, current 50) - DF(t, trailing 200). Peak 30.5% on 'societal', the global maximum of the replay; precision 95.8% (23 of 24 in-window fires are the contaminant) vs maxDF*'s 10.8%; all five register tokens that false-breach today fall below the 25.0% threshold (item 21.5, aligns 19.5, engagement 19.5, systems 19.5, discusses 16.5). Drift cannot break it because the baseline drifts with the register by construction. KNOWN LIMITATION stated up front: a convergence slower than the trailing baseline is absorbed and invisible -- the design trades cannot-track-drift for cannot-see-slow-convergence. CALIBRATION CAVEAT: threshold set on p99 of out-of-window readings from ONE event, n=1; 95.8% is a feasibility signal, not a calibrated FPR. Other candidates NOT prioritised (drift-native subsumed; subject-level blind to R59 scaffolding). NEXT: design round for self-referencing excess with its own pre-registration fixing baseline length, threshold calibration, and the fate of the frozen list.

R66 design round for self-referencing excess, report only, nothing written/deleted; register_exclusion.json, GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md, corpus_convergence.py UNTOUCHED. Pre-registered in a SEPARATE prior commit (24b7078) with a failure clause and an anti-tuning clause. VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS -- recommend B=200, theta=22%, W=50 held fixed; SHIPPING BLOCKED on condition (c) until ~2026-08-17. (a) PASS: clean-corpus FPR 0.00% over 253 windows at B=200, and Gatwick fires at 30.5% vs theta=22% inside the required 20% margin (0.8x30.5=24.4). (b) PASS: T_max = 193 beliefs (2.4 days) vs the pre-registered bar of 2x the Gatwick ramp = 146; Gatwick's ramp measured at 73 beliefs / 1.28 days, so 1.9x margin. HEADLINE BLIND-SPOT COST: at B=200/theta=22% a convergence ramping to 34% DF over more than 2.4 DAYS is invisible. (c) UNDETERMINED at B=200 (disjoint-half test needs ~700 clean docs, have 502) and FAILS at B=100 (26% vs 20%, 6pp against a 4pp bar). Not recorded as a pass. GRID OVER-REACHED, reported not hidden: B=800 not evaluable (0 windows), B=400 low power (53 windows, FPR resolution 1.9%), B=400 injection corpus-limited and invalid. Anti-tuning HELD -- did not add B=150/300 when 100 and 200 straddled the bars. B=100 fails TWO independent conditions, which is the evidence the clause has teeth. RULE-RECONSTRUCTION: the <=1% rule on maxDF*'s own current readings emits 44%, not its shipped 25% -- not a rule defect but an independent measure of 19 points of threshold staleness, corroborating R65's 10.8% precision from another direction. ITEM 3 RE-VERIFIED (not cited): zero importers of corpus_convergence, zero readers of register_exclusion.json outside it, zero cron/systemd. Obsoleted by the replacement: both register_exclusion JSONs entirely; _REGISTER_PATH, load_register_exclusion(), max_df_star(exclusion=). Reusable: recent_crystallized(), WINDOW, CLI scaffolding. GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE Ss5 needs REWRITE not delete -- the failure mode is real and maxDF* does detect it. SEQUENCE: phase 0 wait to ~08-17 and run the (c) check (502/700 docs at a measured 80.3/day); if halves disagree >4pp the design FAILS on threshold instability and the recommendation is withdrawn. Phase 1 implement alongside, 14-day parallel. Phase 2 delete. Deletion is a later round regardless.

R67 pre-registration only, NO test run, no theta computed, nothing written/deleted. Locks the Aug 17-19 (c) stability re-run decision tree while the outcome is unknown. PRECONDITION: brief says >=700 docs; flagged a defect -- at 100 windows/half the FPR estimate steps by 1/100 = 1%, exactly the calibration target, so a single window flips theta and the test would measure quantisation noise and report it as instability. Recommend >=800 (150 windows/half). RESOLVED so neither choice improvises: at >=800 both outcomes conclusive; at 700-799 a PASS is conclusive (a fortiori, passing despite added noise) but a FAIL is NOT and must be re-run at >=800. Never below 700. Conditional on no fire-path change (resets the clean window). Corpus 502 now, 80.3/day measured over 6 full days -> 700 ~08-17, 800 ~08-18/19. BRANCH A (halves agree <=4pp) is NOT clear-to-implement: four gates -- A1 recalibrate theta on the full corpus, A2 recalibrated theta must be within 4pp of 22% else route to Branch B, A3 re-verify Gatwick fires at the NEW theta with 20% margin, A4 re-verify T_max >= 146 at the NEW theta. A3/A4 exist because theta is an input to both and neither direction is automatically safe. Pass all four -> phase 1 parallel run 14 days. BRANCH B (>4pp): B=200 dead. B=400 is NOT tested in the same round -- decided on arithmetic: its full-corpus calibration becomes adequate at 700+ but its disjoint-half STABILITY test needs 1200 docs, and stability is the question. B2 record direction (B=100 was 6pp; <6pp supports longer baselines, >=6pp falsifies the mechanism and skips to B4). B3 schedule B=400 at 1200 docs ~08-23/25 as its own pre-registered round. B4 STOPPING RULE: B=400 is the last candidate -- B=800 needs ~2000 docs ~25 days of single-regime corpus which NEX has never had; if B=400 fails, self-referencing excess is ABANDONED and maxDF* is not resurrected. Anti-tuning: grid stays {100,200,400,800}, 4.5pp is Branch B not "close enough", finer searches are pre-registered AS searches in a later round. TWO DISCLOSURE CORRECTIONS. (1) MECHANISM MISATTRIBUTED in R66: longer baseline is not less blind "because the ramp has less time to contaminate it" -- T_max = p(W+B)/(2theta) scales with (W+B), so a longer baseline reaches further back along the ramp to where the token was rarer. Verdict unchanged, reason was wrong. Live consequence: W and B enter symmetrically, so widening the current window buys exactly what widening the baseline buys (W 50->100 at B=200 gives T_max 232 vs 193) -- W was held fixed all series as a given and was actually a free parameter nobody costed; NOT changed now, scoped to the next design round. (2) GATWICK BASELINE WAS CONTAMINATED, measured: 100% of the trailing baseline inside the contamination window at B=100 and B=200, 60% at B=400; societal DF in baseline 2.0/3.5/1.8% against 34.0% in the current window. Every reported excess is UNDERSTATED; against a clean baseline it is 34.0%. This also explains the non-monotonic peak (32.0/30.5/32.2) -- not a property of B but of how much ramp each lookback absorbed. Margin rule: conservative measured figure retained as the bar (0.8x30.5=24.4 vs theta 22), true clean-baseline bar is 27.2, both disclosed. Ss5 blind-spot line drafted verbatim for the rewrite: a convergence ramping to peak over more than ~2.4 days is invisible at B=200; a quiet reading is evidence of no FAST convergence, not of no convergence.
